en.marketHeading: What is actually different about marketing in {city}
market: {city} is the service centre for southwestern Ontario. The hospital network, the university and the professional services around them draw people in from a catchment several times the size of the city, which means the market you can sell into is much larger than the population figure suggests. A specialist practice, a legal firm or a distributor in {city} that targets only the city limits is competing for a fraction of its own natural market.

That regional pull has a second effect worth planning around. Someone driving 40 minutes into {city} for a service has already decided that local is not good enough, which makes them a considered buyer rather than an impulsive one. They compare, they read, and they arrive with a shortlist. That is a strong argument for putting real work into what they find when they research, rather than relying on being the cheapest click.

The economy underneath is stable in the way institutional economies are. Health care, education and financial services anchor employment, with manufacturing and agriculture across the surrounding counties. Steady demand, moderate competition, and a search market where a well built account can realistically own its category rather than rent a corner of it.

faq.q: Do you have an office in {city}?
faq.a: No. I am based in Toronto and work from home, so there is no {city} office and I am not going to imply there is. Everything is run remotely over video and email, which is how I run every account.

faq.q: How wide should we target around {city}?
faq.a: As wide as people will genuinely travel for what you sell, and no wider. For a restaurant that is a few kilometres. For a specialist clinic, a legal practice or a distributor it can be the better part of southwestern Ontario. Getting this right is worth more than a budget increase in most {city} accounts, and it takes about an hour to work out properly.

faq.q: Which service should a {city} business start with?
faq.a: If your customer has an urgent problem, Google Ads. If your customer researches and compares before travelling into the city, SEO first, because that is where their research actually happens. AIO is cheap, one time, and nearly untouched by your local competitors.

faq.q: Do you work with businesses in the surrounding towns?
faq.a: Yes, on the same terms. Everything is remote so the town makes no difference to the work or the price. Businesses outside the city often have the clearest opportunity, because the competition thins out quickly once you leave {city}.
Google Ads management is $1,500 a month plus your ad spend. SEO consulting is $1,200 a month. AIO consulting is $1,800 one time. No setup fees and no long contract.
